children: U.S. stocks were steady and Treasurys largely strengthened, while the dollar gained against the euro amid concern that French fiscal stress would spread elsewhere on the continent.

Major U.S. stock indexes were little moved after rising sharply Friday, when weak jobs data dimmed market expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes and supported risk assets. Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 were flat, while Nasdaq futures edged 0.1% lower. Asian stocks mostly gained as the continent caught up on Friday's jobs data. Japan's Nikkei climbed 2.4%, while indexes in mainland China, Hong Kong and Korea also gained. European stocks were mixed in volatile early trade, with the Stoxx 600 last rising 0.5%.

Shorter-dated Treasury yields pulled back from highs at the end of last week, though levels remained close to multidecade highs. Two-year Treasury yields fell 1.2 basis points to 4.827%, while 10-year yields nudged 0.9 basis point lower to 5.274%. Yields on 30-year Treasurys continued to rise, however, adding 0.9 basis point to 5.623%.

Political pressures mounted on markets across the globe, with French budget pressures added to by Spanish leader Pedro Sanchez's call for a snap election Monday. In Brazil, the surprise first-round election win for right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro could shake markets in both South America and Europe.

The euro fell to a 16-month low against the U.S. dollar as concern around French government spending started to weigh on the continent's common currency. Spreads between French 10-year yields and German 10-year Bund yields widened, though yields on French bonds held below multidecade highs hit Friday.
"The big question is whether this is the start of a new euro sovereign crisis or whether markets have already overshot," Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid said.

Oil prices nudged higher after Saudi Aramco Chief Executive Amin Nasser said the global supply cushion was "scarily thin," and that inventories could take as long as two years to rebuild. Prices had eased earlier in the session after Saudi Arabia sharply cut the price of its flagship crude grade for Asian buyers. Brent crude contracts for December inched up 0.5% to $102.70 a barrel, while WTI contracts fell 0.9% to trade around $90 a barrel.
Bitcoin and gold both strengthened slightly, with bitcoin adding 0.4% to trade around $86,100. Gold gained 0.5%, but held below $4,200 a troy ounce in New York.

Later Monday, the September ISM services index will help shape market views on the U.S. economy's health. For the week ahead, Fed meeting minutes Wednesday will give investors insight into policymakers' outlook for rates.
